newsitem.title: FRANCE: Peugeot profit tumbles as car price war rages on.
newsitem.headline: Peugeot profit tumbles as car price war rages on.

text.p: France's PSA Peugeot Citroen said on Thursday annual profits tumbled last year as a price war hit French carmakers and said it would cut its dividend.

The carmaker said net attributable profit for 1996 plunged to 734 million francs ($126.3 million) from 1.7 billion francs in the preceding year and that it planned to cut its net dividend to three francs a share from five francs in 1995.

That fell short of even the lower predictions by industry analysts, whose estimates had produced a consensus of 1.2 billion francs net attributable profit and a wide range of 800 million to 1.7 billion.

The group said in a statement that a price war had hit its results and that the fierce competition in the French car market since last autumn showed no sign of abating. Overall French car market sales could fall by 11-12 percent this year, it said.

"The fierce competition raging in Europe does not look like going away," it said. "The Western European car market should see overall growth of close to two percent in 1997 but the depression of the French market since autumn 1996 has continued unabated and sales could recede by 11-12 percent over the year."

As far as Peugeot itself was concerned, the company said: "Nevertheless, bolstered by the success of its car range, notably in the light commercial vehicles sector, PSA Peugeot Citroen sales should meet the target gains which the group has set itself."
Operating profit tumbled to 1.675 billion francs from 3.751 billion francs, while sales had risen to 172.668 billion francs from 164.248 billion the preceding year, it said.
The Peugeot profit news came less than a month after rival Renault announced a loss of 5.25 billion francs, its first loss in 10 years.

Renault is currently embroiled in controversy over its plans to shut down a Belgian factory near Brussels with the loss of nearly 2,800 jobs. This company included charges for this closure in its 1996 results, to the tune of 3.91 billion francs. ($ = 5.810 French Francs)
